description: Committee recommends 1st Avenue BRT changes: with-flow lanes, 4 stations.
This reduces on-street parking by 61 stalls.

chips.text: Midtown Plaza supports changes, citing improved safety and ample off-street parking.
Taxpayers will fund an additional $165,000 annually for snow removal.
Administration seeks committee direction on removing 2nd Avenue median.
Practical snow removal plan during BRT operational hours remains unclear.
Several business groups and residents expressed concerns about parking, access, and safety.

segments.title: Staff Introduction and Project History
segments.takeaway: Terry Schmidt introduces the First Avenue Bus Rapid Transit concept changes, providing historical context of the project and its alignment with the city's growth plan.

segments.title: Consultant Presentation on Design Revisions
segments.takeaway: Seema Plus engineering consultants present detailed design revisions, including changes to lane flow, station locations, and parking, along with road safety audit findings.

segments.title: Snow Removal Plan for BRT Corridor
segments.takeaway: Administration details the proposed snow grading and removal plan for the First Avenue BRT corridor, outlining operational changes and estimated incremental costs.

segments.title: Public Comments on BRT Concept Changes
segments.takeaway: Several community members and business representatives present their views on the proposed BRT changes, discussing impacts on parking, traffic flow, safety, and the consultation process.

segments.title: Committee Break
segments.takeaway: The committee takes a ten-minute break after hearing from all public speakers, before proceeding with questions for administration.

description: Three major construction projects planned for summer 2026.
25th Street water main, University Bridge arch repairs will cause detours.
College Drive link project closes sections for BRT.

chips.text: Mayor Block noted some residents will be unhappy, but work must proceed.
Drivers accessing the University and Jim Patterson Children's Hospitals will face detours.
City commits to maintaining access to University and Jim Patterson Children's Hospitals.
